text: Dua Lipa (/ˈduːə ˈliːpə/ ⓘ DOO-ə LEE-pə; born 22 August 1995) is an English singer and songwriter with seven Brit Awards and three Grammy Awards. Born in London, England, she is the eldest child of Kosovo Albanian parents Anesa (née Rexha) and Dukagjin Lipa from Pristina, FR Yugoslavia (present-day Kosovo), and has a sister, Rina, and a brother, Gjin. The name Dua, suggested by her grandmother, means "love" in Albanian, and her maternal grandmother is of Bosniak descent; both of her grandfathers were historians, with her father's ancestry traced to Peja, Kosovo. Musically influenced by her father, the lead singer and guitarist of the Kosovan rock band Oda, who played music at home including works by David Bowie, Bob Dylan, Radiohead, Sting, the Police, and Stereophonics, Lipa began singing at age five. She attended Fitzjohn's Primary School, where she took cello lessons and was initially told she could not sing in the choir; at nine, she began weekend singing lessons at the Sylvia Young Theatre School. After Kosovo declared independence in 2008, she moved to Pristina, where she attended Mileniumi i Tretë School and considered a music career. At 15, she returned to London alone and shared a flat with a family friend, attending Parliament Hill School to pass her A-Levels and later re-entering Sylvia Young Theatre School part-time. She uploaded songs to SoundCloud and YouTube, covering tracks like "If I Ain't Got You" and "Beautiful." In 2013, she modelled with Topshop, signed with Tap Management (directed by Ben Mawson and Ed Millett), and was introduced to Mawson by her lawyer, who discouraged her from signing another publishing deal. Mawson and Millett offered her a monthly salary to leave her job as a waitress in a cocktail bar to focus on music; during a session, she co-wrote "Hotter than Hell," which led to her signing a record deal with Warner Bros. Records in 2014. In August 2015, she released her first single, "New Love," produced by Emile Haynie and Andrew Wyatt; her second single, "Be the One," reached number one in Belgium, Poland, and Slovakia, charted in the top ten in over eleven European territories, and became an airplay success in Australia and New Zealand. In November 2015, she was named on the BBC Sound of... 2016 long list. Her first tour in the UK and Europe began in January 2016 and concluded in early December 2016. On 18 February 2016, she released "Last Dance," followed by "Hotter than Hell" on 6 May, which peaked at number 15 in the UK; on 26 August, "Blow Your Mind (Mwah)" was released, peaking at number 30 in the UK and becoming her first entry on the US Billboard Hot 100, debuting at number 72, while topping the Billboard Dance Club Songs chart and reaching number 23 on the Billboard Mainstream Top 40 chart. In November 2016, she was featured on Sean Paul's single "No Lie," which reached number ten in the UK and became a top-ten hit in ten countries six years after its release, becoming Sean Paul's most-streamed song as of December 2022, with the music video surpassing 1 billion views on YouTube by April 2022. A documentary about her, See in Blue, was commissioned by The Fader in January 2017. That month, she won the EBBA Public Choice Award and released "Scared to Be Lonely" with Martin Garrix, which reached number 14 in the UK. In May 2017, she performed at the anniversary of Indonesian television channel SCTV and won the award for Young and Promising International Artist at the SCTV Music Awards. Her debut album, Dua Lipa, was released on 2 June 2017; its sixth single, "New Rules," released the following month, became her first number one in the UK, the first by a female solo artist to reach the top since Adele's "Hello" in 2015, and charted in the top ten in Australia (number two), the US (number six), and Canada (number seven). As of 2024, the music video for "New Rules" has streamed over three billion views on YouTube. In June 2017, she performed at the Glastonbury Festival, in July at the We The Fest in Jakarta, and on BBC's Later... with Jools Holland in October. In December 2017, she was named the most streamed woman of 2017 in the UK by Spotify. In 2017, she had four singles reach the UK top 10: "Be the One," "New Rules," "No Lie," and "Bridge over Troubled Water," a charity single for the families of the victims of the Grenfell Tower fire. In January 2018, she received five nominations at the Brit Awards, more than any other artist that year, including British Album of the Year, British Single of the Year, British Video of the Year for "New Rules," British Female Solo Artist, and British Breakthrough Act, winning the latter two—making her the first female artist to receive five nominations. She performed at the awards ceremony on 21 February at the O2 Arena in London. In February 2018, she collaborated with American DJ Whethan on "High" for the Fifty Shades Freed soundtrack. In April 2018, she and Calvin Harris released "One Kiss," which topped the UK Singles Chart on 20 April, making it her second number one, and became the best-selling song of 2018 in the UK, staying at number one for eight consecutive weeks. She performed in the opening ceremony of the 2018 UEFA Champions League Final in Kyiv on 26 May. In September 2018, she performed at the F1 Singapore Grand Prix and endorsed Jaguar's new electric car, the I-PACE; the brand created a remix of her song "Want To" and launched a service allowing fans to create and share their own version of the song on Join the Pace, setting a world record for the "most remixed song ever." In October 2018, she released Dua Lipa: The Complete Edition, an expanded version of her debut album including three new songs, such as "Want To" and a collaboration with South Korean girl group Blackpink titled "Kiss and Make Up." In January 2019, she released "Swan Song" for the film Alita: Battle Angel. That month, she stated she had spent the previous year writing her second studio album, which she described as a "nostalgic" pop record that "feels like a dancercise class." In August 2019, she partnered with Yves Saint Laurent to endorse their fragrance Libre. In December 2019, her second album, Future Nostalgia, and its accompanying tour were announced. The album's lead single, "Don't Start Now," peaked at number two on both the UK Singles Chart and the US Billboard Hot 100, earning the longest top-ten stay for a British female artist on the UK Singles Chart and the longest top-ten stay without reaching number one in that chart's history; it also peaked at number one on the UK Big Top 40 and the US Billboard Mainstream Top 40 chart. Her second single leading up to the album's release was "Physical," released on 30 January 2020, with the music video released the next day; it debuted at number 60 on the US Billboard Hot 100. Future Nostalgia was released on 27 March to widespread critical acclaim, following the release of the record's third single, "Break My Heart," on 25 March. The album debuted at number two on the Official UK Albums Chart, 5550 copies behind 5 Seconds of Summer's Calm, and peaked at number one the following week in April 2020, while four of its singles entered the top ten of the Official Singles Chart. The album holds the record for the lowest one-week sales while at number one in the 21st century, with only 7,317 sales during the week beginning 15 May 2020. At the time of release, Lipa became the first British female artist since Vera Lynn to have three top-ten singles in a single calendar year, with Lynn having three in 1952; she later surpassed this with "Levitating," which also peaked within the top ten on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming her third top-ten in the US overall. The music video for "Physical" was nominated for Best Art Director at the Berlin Music Video Awards in 2020, with Anna Colomer Nogué as the art director. On 27 April 2020, DJ Ben Howell released a remix of "Hallucinate" with the BBC news theme, created during the coronavirus lockdown in Glasgow, Scotland, which garnered over a million views on YouTube by July 2023 and was well-received by Lipa and BBC Radio 1 DJ Greg James. On 11 August 2020, she was named global ambassador of the French mineral water brand Évian. On 13 August, she released a remix of "Levitating" featuring Madonna and Missy Elliott, which served as the lead single from Club Future Nostalgia, a remix collection of Future Nostalgia tracks by the Blessed Madonna and Mark Ronson, released on 28 August. On 2 October 2020, she released a second remix of "Levitating" featuring DaBaby, along with the music video for the remix. On 14 October 2020, she and Belgian singer Angèle were photographed on the set of a music video; later that month, they announced their collaboration, "Fever," released on 30 October 2020 and included on the French re-release of Future Nostalgia. In November 2020, she was featured on "Prisoner," a song from Miley Cyrus' Plastic Hearts album, released on 19 November with a music video. In November, it was announced she would be the musical guest on the 19 December episode of Saturday Night Live. On 27 November, she performed in a livestream concert titled Studio 2054, where she sang songs from Future Nostalgia, a new unreleased track with FKA Twigs, and previous singles such as "New Rules," "One Kiss," and "Electricity," featuring special guests including the Blessed Madonna, Angèle, Kylie Minogue, and Elton John. Lipa and Belgian singer Angèle were photographed on the set of a music video. Later in the month, the singers announced the release of their collaboration, "Fever," which was released on 30 October 2020 and is included on the French re-release of Future Nostalgia. Lipa was featured on "Prisoner," a song from Miley Cyrus' seventh studio album Plastic Hearts, released on 19 November 2020 alongside its music video. In November, it was announced that Lipa would be the musical guest on the 19 December episode of Saturday Night Live. On 27 November, Lipa performed in a livestream concert titled Studio 2054, where she sang various songs from Future Nostalgia, a new unreleased track with FKA Twigs, as well as previous singles such as "New Rules," "One Kiss," and "Electricity." The event featured special guests including the Blessed Madonna, Angèle, Kylie Minogue, and Elton John. Future Nostalgia was the most streamed album by a woman (and fifth most streamed album overall) on Spotify in 2020. On 11 February 2021, Lipa released a single titled "We're Good" along with Future Nostalgia: The Moonlight Edition. On 26 February 2021, Aleyna Tilki released her debut English-language single "Retrograde," co-written by Lipa. Lipa released the song "Can They Hear Us" from the soundtrack of the film Gully on 4 June 2021. On 13 August 2021, Lipa worked again with Elton John on the song "Cold Heart (Pnau remix)," released as the lead single from John's studio album The Lockdown Sessions, which reached number one on the UK Singles Chart on 15 October, becoming Lipa's third song to achieve this feat. In February 2022, Lipa launched a weekly lifestyle newsletter entitled Service95 and its accompanying podcast Dua Lipa: At Your Service. On 18 February 2022, a source close to the issue confirmed to Variety that Dua Lipa had parted ways with her longtime management business, Ben Mawson and Ed Millet's TaP Management, though the insider claimed she is not currently meeting with other management firms but will do so in the future. On 1 March 2022, reggae band Artikal Sound System filed a suit against Lipa and her label Warner Records alleging copyright infringement, asserting similarities between "Levitating" and their 2017 song "Live Your Life," which was dropped with prejudice in June 2023. A second suit by songwriters L. Russell Brown and Sandy Linzer claimed that "Levitating" infringed on their 1979 disco song "Wiggle and Giggle All Night." On 11 March 2022, Lipa and Megan Thee Stallion released "Sweetest Pie" accompanied by its music video, marking their first collaboration and serving as the lead single from Megan's second studio album Traumazine. On 27 May, Lipa collaborated with Calvin Harris and Young Thug to release "Potion," serving as the lead single from Harris's sixth studio album Funk Wav Bounces Vol. 2, marking the second collaboration between Harris and Lipa following their 2018 single "One Kiss." On 26 May 2023, Lipa released "Dance the Night" as the lead single of the Barbie film soundtrack, making her acting debut in the movie as Mermaid Barbie. In November 2023, Lipa acquired full ownership of all her songs, music, and publishing rights in a new deal completed with her former music publishers, TaP Music, which included all of her master recordings from her entire music catalogue, reaching 40 billion streams by February 2024. On 9 November 2023, Lipa released the lead single from her third studio album titled "Houdini," stating that Kevin Parker, who produced the song with Danny L Harle, was among her "core collaborators" on the album, with Spin referring to Harle as the co-producer. The follow-up singles "Training Season" and "Illusion" were released on 15 February 2024 and 11 April 2024, respectively, with the album Radical Optimism following on 3 May 2024. She continued her acting career with a starring role in the 2024 spy action comedy Argylle. In March 2024, Dua Lipa announced a short tour of European arenas in June of the same year, performing at the Arena of Nîmes, the Waldbühne in Berlin, and the Pula Arena, all of which are amphitheatres. In June, she headlined at Glastonbury Festival 2024, closing the festival's Pyramid Stage on 28 June. On 18 March 2024, Lipa announced the Radical Optimism Tour, a concert tour in support of the album. On 17 October, she performed at the Royal Albert Hall in London for an ITV television special titled An Evening with Dua Lipa, where she sang her biggest hits and songs from Radical Optimism, backed by the Heritage Orchestra. A remix of "These Walls" featuring Belgian singer Pierre de Maere was released as the fourth single from Radical Optimism on 8 November 2024. On 19 November, she announced the release of her first live album titled Dua Lipa Live from the Royal Albert Hall for 6 December, preceding the broadcast of An Evening with Dua Lipa on 8 December. Lipa has been the cover girl of several magazines. She signed with Next Models. She was on the cover of the "Boom Boom Tick" editorial for Elle's January 2016 issue. In April 2016, she was again in an editorial of Elle. She was on a supplemental cover of British Vogue in November 2016. She starred an editorial for the January 2017 issue of V. In the same month, she was on the cover for issue 102 of Clash. In March 2017, she became a global ambassador for the American shoe company Foot Locker to present women's collections offered by the brand. She was in an editorial for Interview released in April 2017. She modelled for an editorial of Paper, published on 6 June 2017. She was featured in the summer 2017 issue of Teen Vogue in an editorial titled "Fine Tuned." She was in an editorial for the June 2017 issue of InStyle. She was in an editorial called "Game Changers" for the Fall 2017 issue of V. She was in the Fall/Winter 2017–18 advertising campaign of the Italian brand Patrizia Pepe, as well as recorded a cover of the song "Bang Bang (My Baby Shot Me Down)" (1966) as a soundtrack for the commercial for the said campaign. She was on the cover and appeared in an editorial for the November 2017 issue of Evening Standard. In the same month, she released her second collaboration with the brand Foot Locker for the autumn/winter collection. In January 2018, she was part of a promotional clip for an Adidas Originals campaign called "Original Is Never Finished." She was on the cover of the April 2018 issue of Teen Vogue. She was on one of the covers for issue 113 of V entitled "The Music Issue," published in May 2018 as a limited edition. She partnered with the fashion brand Nyden on a project to create four clothing collections, but it failed and Lipa "discontinued" her work with the brand. She was on the cover of British GQ for the May 2018 issue. She was in the cover for the May 2018 issue of the Turkish edition of Vogue. She was in the cover for the June 2018 issue of the British edition of Elle. In October 2018, she was part of an Adidas campaign called "Here to Create" in which she wore brand clothes. She appeared in a Billboard editorial called "Grammy Preview" alongside Post Malone and Ella Mai. She starred the cover for the January 2019 issue of British Vogue and an editorial called "Youth Quake." She was the image for the Pepe Jeans London spring/summer 2019 collection campaign, settling down as the first musician to be global ambassador for the brand. Months later she launched her first-ever capsule with the same brand for the autumn/winter collection where she designed clothing inspired by the fashion of the 90s and early 2000s. She had spent part of her childhood in London and remembered her mother talking to her in a Pepe Jeans store in Portobello Road; the collection included chain mail dresses, "casual" denim outfits and garments based on Lipa's "style" released in September 2019. She was on the cover of the May 2019 issue of Elle. She starred one of the four covers in the first issue and an editorial of the re-launch of The Face released in September 2019. She was the cover girl of the October 2019 issue and an editorial for the Spanish edition of Vogue. She starred in a Vogue sitcom clip set in the 90s titled "Dua's World" where she wore the "best" collections of New York Fashion Week. She released her second design collaboration with Pepe Jeans London for the spring/summer 2020 collection inspired by the fashion of the late 1980s and early 1990s, whose collection included "oversized" blazers, cropped knitwear, bodycon dresses, and "metallic" miniskirts. She was on the cover and an editorial called "True to form" for the April 2020 issue of Vogue Australia. She appeared in a Rolling Stone editorial published in April 2020 to discuss her second studio album Future Nostalgia (2020). She was on the cover of the Elle May 2020 issue and an editorial titled "Dua Lipa Gets Physical," and months later she was in the cover for its Canadian and British edition. She was the cover girl for the June 2020 issue of GQ on its British edition. She was on one of two covers for W's "The Music Issue," published in September 2020. Lipa released her third design collaboration with Pepe Jeans London for the autumn/winter 2020 collection and stated that it would be her last collaboration with the brand called "Denim decades," which was inspired by every decade since Pepe Jeans started selling denim. In November 2020, she signed a multi-year partnership with Puma becoming the global ambassador of the brand. She was on the cover for the December 2020 issue of Attitude. She appeared on the cover for the February 2021 issue of British Vogue. In the same month, she was protagonist of the cover for issue 1348 of Rolling Stone. She was on the cover for the March 2021 issue of Time, representing the 100 Next list about the "future 100 most influential people in the world." In the same month, she appeared on the cover of The New York Times "Music Issue." She designed her outfit at the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards red carpet featuring a dress in collaboration with the brand Versace inspired by the Aurora Borealis. She was in a Puma brand campaign called "She Moves Us" in which she designed a shoe called "Mayze" released in April 2021. In June 2021, Lipa was announced as the face of Versace's Fall-Winter 2021 campaign. Dua Lipa has been described by the media as a fashion icon. For a Versace dress and Bulgari diamonds she was rated as one of the "best" dressed celebrities of the 61st Annual Grammy Awards ceremony by various media. For her Alexander Wang dress with 90s style, she was rated as one of the "best" dressed celebrities of the 62nd Annual Grammy Awards ceremony. For a Versace dress and Bulgari jewellery she was rated as one of the "best" dressed celebrities of the 63rd Annual Grammy Awards ceremony. She released a limited edition lip gloss called "Cremesheen Glass" in collaboration with MAC Cosmetics for its campaign called "Future Forward." She became the face of a perfume called "Libre" for a Yves Saint Laurent campaign launched in September 2019 for which she recorded a promo cover of the song "I'm Free" (1965) featured in advertisements for Lipa's campaigns with the brand. Later she was the face of a new version of the same perfume called "Libre Intense." She became an ambassador for the mineral water brand Évian in July 2020. In March 2021 she performed an a cappella of her song "Levitating" (2020) for an advertisement for the "Drink True" campaign of the brand Évian. In February 2024, Dua Lipa was promoted to global ambassador for YSL Beauty. Previously, she had been the face of the "Libre" fragrance since 2019. Her appointment to global ambassador followed a wipe of the YSL Beauty Instagram account. She made her runway debut at Versace's Spring/Summer 2022 show at Milan Fashion Week, which was soundtracked by tracks from her album Future Nostalgia (2020). The media have described Lipa as having a mezzo-soprano or contralto vocal range. Her music is primarily pop, and has also been described as disco and house with elements of R&B. Stylistically, her music has been described as dance-pop, synth-pop, dream pop, alternative pop, and nu-disco subgenres. She describes her musical style as being "dark pop." She is also noted for singing in a "distinct, husky, low register," and her "sultry" tone. Regarding her songwriting process, Lipa states she usually comes to the studio with a concept and starts developing the song with her co-writers. She cites Kylie Minogue, Pink, Nelly Furtado, Jamiroquai, Prince, Kendrick Lamar, and Chance the Rapper among her musical influences. "My idea of pop has been P!nk and Christina Aguilera and Destiny's Child and Nelly Furtado," said Lipa in a GQ interview in 2018. Her second studio album Future Nostalgia (2020) was inspired by artists that she listened to during her teens, including Gwen Stefani, Madonna, Moloko, Blondie, and Outkast. Lipa's stage presence was met with criticism in the early stages of her career. A YouTube comment on her performance of "New Rules" at the 2018 BRIT Awards saying "I love her lack of energy, go girl give us nothing" became an internet meme, subjecting Lipa to ridicule. Dua Lipa co-wrote her songs with her co-writers and cites Kylie Minogue, Pink, Nelly Furtado, Jamiroquai, Prince, Kendrick Lamar, and Chance the Rapper as musical influences. In a 2018 GQ interview, she stated that her idea of pop includes P!nk, Christina Aguilera, Destiny's Child, and Nelly Furtado. Her second studio album, Future Nostalgia (2020), was inspired by artists she listened to during her teens, such as Gwen Stefani, Madonna, Moloko, Blondie, and Outkast. Early in her career, her stage presence drew criticism, exemplified by a YouTube comment on her "New Rules" BRIT Awards performance that became an internet meme, which she credited as motivation to improve. A study by the Office for National Statistics found that the number of people born with the name "Dua" in England and Wales rose from 63 in 2017 to 126 in 2019, the year she earned her first UK number-one with "New Rules." In May 2018, she was named one of British Vogue’s 25 most influential British women of 2018 at age 22, with the review calling "New Rules" an "anthem of female empowerment" and describing her as a "culture definer." Lyndsey Havens of Billboard credited her with leading the revival of disco in 2020 through "Don't Start Now" (2019), and she was dubbed "the Future of Pop" due to the success of Future Nostalgia. She inspired French photographer Hugo Comte’s first photo-book and was included in Time’s 100 Next list by Kylie Minogue, who called her a "shining star." Mark Sutherland and Jem Aswad of Variety rated her one of the most impactful women in global entertainment. Wax figures of Dua Lipa are displayed at Madame Tussauds in major cities worldwide. She has won seven Brit Awards from nineteen nominations, three Grammy Awards from ten, two MTV Video Music Awards from twenty-three, two MTV Europe Music Awards from sixteen, two American Music Awards from seven, three iHeartRadio Music Awards from nineteen, nine Spotify 1 billion streams plaques, and one Bambi Award. She holds two Guinness World Records: in 2020 for most tickets sold for a livestreamed concert by a solo female artist, and in 2021 for most monthly listeners on Spotify for a female artist, though she did not surpass Ariana Grande’s prior peak. In 2024, she won the Top Dance/Electronic Song award at the Billboard Music Awards for "Houdini," which topped the Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart for 17 weeks. Time included her in its 2024 Time 100 list of the world’s most influential people, and Billboard ranked her number 25 on its 2025 "Top 100 Women Artists of the 21st Century" list. Lipa identifies as a feminist and has spoken out against sexism in the music industry and advocated for social equality in the LGBT community. On 12 February 2018, she raised a rainbow flag during a performance of "Be the One" at the Hollywood Palladium as part of The Self-Titled tour. At the 2018 Brit Awards red carpet, she wore a white rose dress in support of the Time's Up movement and stated in her acceptance speech her delight at women being present and winning awards, clarifying that her feminism is about equal opportunities, not misandry. In September 2018, some fans were removed from a Shanghai concert for waving rainbow flags, despite homosexuality being decriminalized in China in 1997; Lipa expressed pride and gratitude for their visibility. In November 2018, she criticized Brexit, stating that no refugee leaves without having to, based on her personal experience. In June 2019, she publicly supported Sudan’s democratic transition by sharing a "Stand with Sudan" image, rejecting the Khartoum massacre as an act of "brutal murder and rape" and a violation of freedom and human rights. In December 2019, she endorsed the Labour Party led by Jeremy Corbyn, calling the election "the most important in a generation" and describing Boris Johnson’s victory as a "total disaster." She participated in a Global Feminism short film directed by Annie Lennox’s The Circle, released ahead of International Women’s Day to raise awareness of misogyny, rape, and violence against women. In April 2019, she called for a boycott of the Sultan of Brunei’s hotel interests after Brunei’s penal code introduced death penalties for homosexuality. At a Billboard Women in Music event, she used her Powerhouse Award speech to highlight ongoing gender inequality, criticized the lack of diversity in the Billboard Hot 100, and encouraged young girls to be "powerhouses of the future." Lipa was the headliner party host for the 2020 Sydney Gay and Lesbian Mardi Gras parade and performed several songs. In July 2020, she signed an open letter to the UK government, delivered to then Minister for Women and Equalities Liz Truss, requesting the banning of conversion therapy. She supports universal health care, noting that in the UK, the National Health Service is considered a right. In June 2020, she criticized the Israel Defense Forces’ treatment of Palestinians and referred to "fake Jews" and "fake Christians" in the Israeli government and U.S. midwest, claiming they created Hamas to justify occupation and oppression. An Im Tirtzu petition with over three thousand signatories demanded that Lipa’s songs be banned from Israeli Army Radio and Galgalatz due to what they called antisemitism and conspiracy theories; the radio responded that it does not boycott artists. In July 2020, she supported the "Let the Music Play" campaign, sending an open letter to Culture Secretary Oliver Dowden urging government support for the UK live music industry’s economic losses during the pandemic. On 18 July 2020, she posted explaining "why Kosovo is not and will never be Serbia," urging a petition for Apple to map Kosovo as an independent state. The next day, she shared an irredentist map of Greater Albania, which is commonly associated with extreme Albanian nationalism, leading to accusations of ethnic nationalism and fascism; she later stated the post was misinterpreted and that she rejects ethnic separatism. In August 2020, she urged her followers to vote against Donald Trump. After supporting Bernie Sanders in the 2020 Democratic primaries, she expressed support for Joe Biden during a virtual event for Albanian Americans, arguing Kosovars owed support to Biden for opposing the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia. In January 2021, she called on Kosovo citizens to vote in the 2021 parliamentary election. In May 2021, she criticized The New York Times for an advertisement that labeled her and others as antisemitic. In July 2021, through her Sunny Hill Foundation, she joined Tirana’s "Adopt a Kindergarten" initiative to rebuild a kindergarten damaged in the 2019 Albania earthquake; the project was completed in October 2021 and named "Sunny Hill Kindergarten." She has raised awareness of the Taliban’s 2021 takeover of Afghanistan through social media and her lifestyle newsletter Service95. In August 2022, she was named an Honorary Ambassador of Kosovo by President Vjosa Osmani, stating it was an honor to represent her country and supporting Kosovans’ right to visa liberalization, freedom to travel, and to dream big. On 13 November 2022, she denied reports of performing at the 2022 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony, criticizing Qatar’s human rights record. In October 2023, she signed an open letter with 185 other artists for the "Artists4Ceasefire" campaign, urging President Biden to push for a ceasefire and humanitarian corridor in Gaza. She and her father, Dukagjin, co-founded the Sunny Hill Foundation in 2016 to help people in Kosovo facing financial hardship. In August 2018, she organized the Sunny Hill Festival to raise funds, receiving the Pristina Key from then-Mayor Shpend Ahmeti, the first time the award was given. In 2019, she hosted the festival again with Miley Cyrus as a performer. In mid-November 2018, she participated in UNICEF’s "Go Blue" campaign on World Children’s Day, re-recording "Be the One" with the word "red" changed to "blue" to promote children’s rights. In December 2018, she performed at a benefit concert for Ellie Goulding’s "Streets of London" event at Wembley Arena, which funds homeless support and raises awareness. In April 2019, she became a UNICEF supporter during a visit to a refugee camp in Beirut, Lebanon, including Bourj el-Barajneh, where she visited Syrian and Palestinian youth lacking adequate health and education. She later supported a campaign with her management to raise £100,000 for charities like The Black Dog and CALM. Lipa called attention to the high suicide rates among women in the arts, stating they are nearly 70% higher than the global average and described mental health as the "issue of our generation." Following the 2019 Albania earthquake, on 26 November 2019, she asked fans to donate and co-released a limited edition "Pray for Albania" t-shirt line with Albanian designers, with all proceeds going to victims. On 15 March 2020, she urged donations to the UNHCR for refugees, calling them the most vulnerable due to crowded living and limited health services. On the same day, she performed "Don't Start Now" on The Late Late Show with James Corden’s "Home Fest" special to raise funds for CDC and Feed the Children. On 16 May 2020, she performed "Break My Heart" on the "Graduate Together: America Honors the High School Class of 2020" special for students whose graduations and proms were canceled. At the end of May 2020, she participated in a digital event "Dream with Us" to raise funds for COVID-19 relief. She contributed a cover of "Times Like These" to BBC Radio 1’s Live Lounge on 23 April 2020 as part of a charity supergroup, Live Lounge Allstars, with profits going to Children in Need, Comic Relief, and the COVID-19 Solidarity Response Fund. She encouraged Lebanese citizens to donate blood after the 2020 Beirut explosion. She donated 5,000 euros to the Theatre of Dodona to establish its own ticketing system and website. She participated in a charity raffle with Belgian singer Angèle and KickCancer Foundation, offering a manuscript of "Don't Start Now" as a prize. She performed virtually at the 2021 Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Award Party, which raised $3 million for the AIDS Foundation. Lipa is occasionally affectionate.

On 23 April 2020, Dua Lipa participated in the Live Lounge segment and was part of the charity supergroup Live Lounge Allstars, where each member recorded and filmed their contribution from their respective households to promote social distancing. Profits from the single were primarily directed to Children in Need, Comic Relief, and the COVID-19 Solidarity Response Fund. She used social media to encourage Lebanese citizens to donate blood to victims affected by the 2020 Beirut explosion. She donated 5,000 euros to the Theatre of Dodona to enable the venue to develop its own ticket system and website. Lipa was involved in an initiative organized by Belgian singer Angèle and the KickCancer Foundation, which included a charity raffle where she offered a manuscript of her song "Don't Start Now" (2019) as a prize. She performed virtually at the 2021 Elton John AIDS Foundation Academy Award Party to benefit the AIDS Foundation in the fight against HIV disease, an event that raised US$3 million. Lipa is occasionally affectionately referred to as 'Dula Peep' by fans, a nickname that originated from a mispronunciation by American talk show host Wendy Williams in 2018 and which she has since positively embraced. She has described herself as an "honorary Liverpool supporter" after her song "One Kiss" was adopted by the football club's fans following her performance at the 2018 UEFA Champions League final and became a club anthem after significant victories. On 27 November 2022, Lipa was granted Albanian citizenship by President Bajram Begaj, one day before Albania's 110th independence celebrations. On 31 July 2025, she was granted Kosovar citizenship by President Vjosa Osmani. She speaks Albanian fluently and has described her "dual identity" as her "strength". Lipa started dating English chef Isaac Carew in 2015; they were together until early 2017, got back together in January 2018, and split for the second time in June 2019. From July 2019 to December 2021, she was in a relationship with American model Anwar Hadid. In 2023, she dated French film director Romain Gavras. Since January 2024, she has been dating British actor Callum Turner. She formally announced their engagement during her July 2025 cover story with British Vogue, following a period of media rumors. Lipa was included in the Sunday Times Rich List for 2024 with an estimated net worth of £90 million.
